questions.question: Bhavnath Mahadev fair is held every year in which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The Bhavnath Mahadev Fair is held every year in Junagarh, Gujarat, at the foot of Mount Girnar.
  • Timing: It takes place during the Maha Shivratri festival in the Hindu month of Magha.
  • Key Feature: The fair is famous for the procession of Naga Sadhus (naked holy men) who take a holy dip in the 'Mrigi Kund' before offering prayers at the Bhavnath temple.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as a day of mourning among the Muslim community?
questions.solution:
Muharram is observed as a day of mourning by the Muslim community, particularly Shias, to commemorate the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (the grandson of Prophet Muhammad).
  • Event: It marks the anniversary of the Battle of Karbala.
  • Observance: It is not a festival of celebration; instead, it involves mourning rituals, processions, and Majlis (gatherings) to remember the sacrifice of Hussain and his family.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the 'Mozart of Madras'?
questions.solution:
The world-renowned music composer AR Rahman is famously known as the 'Mozart of Madras'.
  • Achievements: He is a pioneer in integrating Eastern classical music with electronic music sounds and world music.
  • Awards: He won two Academy Awards (Oscars) for the film Slumdog Millionaire and has received multiple Grammys, BAFTAs, and National Film Awards.

questions.question: Who among the following founded his Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras in 1963?
questions.solution:
Vempati Chinna Satyam was a legendary dancer who founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Madras (now Chennai) in 1963.
  • Impact: He is credited with refining the Kuchipudi dance form, giving it a more classical structure and popularizing it globally.
  • Legacy: He choreographed over 180 solo items and 15 dance dramas, training generations of famous dancers.

questions.question: Which of the following Khayal artists is the founding father of Lalit Kala Kendra of the University of Pune?
questions.solution:
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, a doyen of the Kirana Gharana, was instrumental in the founding of the Lalit Kala Kendra (Gurukul) at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
  • Genre: He was a master of Khayal singing and is famous for his Bhajans and Abhangs.
  • Honors: He was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 2008.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT figure among the themes of 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav'?
questions.solution:
Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an initiative to celebrate 75 years of progressive India. The five specific themes are:
  1. Freedom Struggle
  2. Ideas@75
  3. Resolve@75
  4. Actions@75
  5. Achievements@75
Health@75 is not one of the official themes of this mahotsav.

questions.question: At which of the following places is the Lalbagh Flower Show organised, where thousands of flower varieties are put on display in different forms with a particular theme (which changes every year) during the exhibition?
questions.solution:
The Lalbagh Flower Show is a prestigious biannual event held in Bengaluru, Karnataka.
  • Venue: It takes place at the Lalbagh Botanical Garden, which features a famous 19th-century Glass House.
  • Timing: It is organized twice a year—during Republic Day (January) and Independence Day (August) weeks.

questions.question: A regal ceremony in the form of Beating Retreat ceremony on the evening of _____________ marks the end of Republic Day celebrations.
questions.solution:
The Beating Retreat ceremony takes place on the evening of 29th January.
  • Significance: It officially denotes the conclusion of the four-day Republic Day celebrations.
  • Participants: It features performances by the bands of the three wings of the Indian Military: the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

questions.question: The national animal of Nepal is:
questions.solution:
The Cow is the national animal of Nepal.
  • Cultural Context: In Nepal, the cow is considered sacred and is associated with the goddess Lakshmi.
  • Legal Status: It was officially declared the national animal in the 2015 Constitution, and its slaughter is strictly prohibited by law.

questions.question: Which famous monument of Vijayapura has a Whispering Gallery, where subtle sounds can be heard clearly even from a distance of 37 metres?
questions.solution:
Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura (Bijapur), Karnataka, is the mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah.
  • Whispering Gallery: Located inside the dome, it is designed such that even a faint whisper is echoed seven to eleven times.
  • Architecture: It is one of the largest single-chamber structures in the world, built in the Indo-Islamic style.

questions.question: The revival of the art form in the late 1940s was spearheaded by maestros such as Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta in the field of ____________.
questions.solution:
The classical dance form Odissi underwent a major revival in the late 1940s led by maestros like Kelucharan Mohapatra.
  • History: Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha. It faced a decline during British rule but was reconstructed using archaeological evidence from temples like Konark.
  • Key Elements: It is characterized by the Tribhanga posture (three-fold bending of the body).

questions.question: Every year, Karthik Purnima marks the end of a livestock fair in Pushkar, where the main animal on display is:
questions.solution:
The Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela) is one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs.
  • Timing: It starts during the month of Kartik and ends on Kartik Purnima.
  • Activities: Apart from trading camels and horses, the fair features competitions such as the 'longest moustache' and 'bridal competition'.

questions.question: Chhath Puja falls in which month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
Chhath Puja is celebrated in the Hindu month of Kartika, specifically on the Shukla Paksha Shashthi (sixth day of the waxing moon).
  • Occasion: It usually occurs six days after Diwali.
  • Deity: It is dedicated to Surya (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya.

questions.question: According to the Indian calendar, the March and April months are known as ___________.
questions.solution:
According to the Hindu Luni-Solar calendar, the months of March and April roughly correspond to Chaitra and Vaisakha.
  • Chaitra: Generally begins in mid-March and marks the start of the Hindu New Year.
  • Vaisakha: Follows Chaitra and is associated with harvest festivals like Baisakhi.

questions.question: Which of the following is the national fruit of Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is the national fruit of Sri Lanka.
  • Significance: It is highly valued for its nutritional content and versatility in Sri Lankan cuisine, often referred to as a 'meat substitute' for its texture.
  • Note: The Jackfruit is also the national fruit of Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which brick-made minaret holds the record for being the world's tallest tower at 73 metres?
questions.solution:
The Qutb Minar in Delhi holds the record for being the world's tallest brick minaret at approximately 73 metres.
  • Construction: It was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192 and completed by his successor Iltutmish.
  • Status: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is a prime example of early Indo-Islamic Afghan architecture.
